bugs: Order::markAsPaid (app/Models/Order.php:43) checks the in-memory status with no lock or conditional update. Two stale instances of the same order both dispatch the job (probe confirmed 2 pushes), and the job has no WithoutOverlapping, so two workers could both POST. Only the Idempotency-Key header stands between that and a duplicate shipment.
A 201 without an id throws (SendOrderToWarehouse.php:104-106), so the job retries and POSTs again even though the partner may already have created the shipment. Probe confirmed 2 POSTs.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:22: the explanatory comment is borderline. It is useful, but it runs long.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:51-55: nested ifs that could be one condition (impl-2/4 write it as `&&`).
Extra shipment_notified_at column and fillable entry not in the spec. Reasonable, but undocumented ceremony.
strengths: Uses modern Laravel 13 queue attributes (#[Timeout, Backoff, MaxExceptions, DeleteWhenMissingModels]), the Foundation Queueable trait, the #[Fillable] attribute and enum casts.
Account-wide RateLimited('warehouse') with Limit::perSecond(5). retryUntil bounds total time while MaxExceptions bounds real errors.
429 releases the job honouring Retry-After. 5xx and timeouts throw into backoff. 422 records the reason and completes without retrying.
Claims the email atomically (conditional update on shipment_notified_at) before sending and rolls the claim back if sending fails, which gives true exactly-once.
dispatch()->afterCommit inside DB::transaction. failed() never overwrites an existing shipment.
Very thorough Pest tests: withFakeQueueInteractions assertReleased(delay: 7), a serialize round-trip for cancellation, mail-failure recovery and idempotency.

bugs: Order::markAsPaid (app/Models/Order.php:39-50) has no idempotency guard. Calling it on an already-shipped order resets shipment_status to pending and dispatches again. The job then skips creation because a reference exists, so the order stays 'pending' forever despite having a shipment (probe confirmed). Every repeated call (e.g. a retried webhook) also queues another job.
notifyCustomer (SendOrderToWarehouse.php:121-127) sends first and records shipment_notified_at afterwards with no atomic claim. A crash or failed save between the two re-sends the email on retry.
429 is thrown as an exception (no Retry-After handling), so partner throttling eats into MaxExceptions(10) and uses the fixed backoff.
A 201 without an id throws and retries, so it re-POSTs (probe: 2 requests).
Without #[DeleteWhenMissingModels], a hard-deleted order turns into a failed job instead of being dropped.
antipatterns: app/Models/Order.php:41-46: unconditional forceFill in markAsPaid, which also clears the failure reason. That hides a state-machine decision inside a payment method.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:116: treats every 4xx except 408/429 as permanent with $this->fail(). That is acceptable, but a 401 from a misconfigured token fails every order permanently.
forceFill used throughout even though the attributes are fillable (except shipment_notified_at).
strengths: Modern attributes (#[Backoff], #[MaxExceptions], #[Timeout], #[Fillable]), enums, and the Foundation Queueable trait.
WithoutOverlapping per order plus a global RateLimited, an Idempotency-Key header, and connect/read timeouts.
Permanent rejection goes through $this->fail(), so failed() records the reason in one place.
Tests cover transaction rollback, a 429/5xx dataset, mail failure and a serialize round-trip for cancellation. Http::preventStrayRequests is set in Pest.php.

bugs: The job never checks that the order is paid (SendOrderToWarehouse.php:50-66). Dispatching it for a pending order ships it (probe confirmed a POST).

markAsPaid (app/Models/Order.php:42) uses a non-atomic in-memory guard. Two stale instances each dispatch a job (probe confirmed 2 pushes). WithoutOverlapping plus refresh() keeps this from producing a double POST, though.
429 is thrown as a generic RequestException: Retry-After is ignored and throttling counts toward MaxExceptions(8).
A 201 without an id throws and retries, so it re-POSTs (probe: 2 requests).
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:58-64: checks shipment_status twice around a void createShipment() that mutates $this->order. The bool-return style of impl-1/2/4 is clearer.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:32: the docblock says releases don't count as exceptions, which is standard framework behaviour.
strengths: refresh() at the start of handle reads the latest state, and the soft-deleted check is reliable.
Http::baseUrl, modern variadic #[Backoff], #[DeleteWhenMissingModels], WithoutOverlapping and RateLimited, and a 2h retryUntil.
Exactly-once email via an atomic claim with rollback on failure.
Markdown mailable using <x-mail::message>.
Good tests: configurable URL, sync-driver failure that reaches failed(), outage recovery and mail-retry isolation.

bugs: notifyCustomer (SendOrderToWarehouse.php:139-148) sends before recording shipment_notified_at, with no atomic claim, so a crash between the two re-sends the email. WithoutOverlapping prevents the concurrent case only.
markAsPaid uses withTrashed (Order.php:54), so a cancelled order can be marked paid and get a job queued. The job then correctly skips it, so this is harmless but sloppy.
Every non-5xx/408/429 4xx is permanent. A 401 from a bad token marks every order failed with no automatic retry. Arguable, but ops can see it.
antipatterns: app/Models/Order.php:19-27: string constants instead of backed enums with enum casts. This is not current Laravel style.

app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:7-22: the legacy Dispatchable/InteractsWithQueue/Queueable/SerializesModels quartet instead of Illuminate\Foundation\Queue\Queueable, and public properties instead of queue attributes ($deleteWhenMissingModels, $maxExceptions, $timeout).
app/Models/Order.php:13: #[UseFactory] is redundant alongside HasFactory's convention.
app/Models/Order.php:66-69: forceFill()->syncOriginal() after a query update is ceremony to mirror state.
Comment density above the rest of the app (Order.php:47-50, Job:26,29-30,33,60, AppServiceProvider:25), some of it narrating the design.
strengths: Atomic, idempotent markAsPaid via a conditional update (where status = pending). It is the only implementation without the double-dispatch race (probe passed).
handle() does a scoped Order::query()->find(), so cancelled orders read as null, and it checks the paid status.
A 201 without an id is recorded as failed rather than retried. This deliberately avoids a duplicate shipment.
429 honours Retry-After, capped at 120s. 5xx/408/timeouts throw into backoff. recordFailure is guarded by whereNull('shipment_reference').
WithoutOverlapping per order plus account-wide RateLimited.
Strongest tests: a real rate-limit test (7 dispatches, frozen time, 5 sent, travel 1s), DB-queue afterCommit rollback, assertReleased(delay: 7) and a 401 path.

v.rationale:
All four suites pass (25, 22, 20 and 24 tests). Each implementation got 7 shared probes, run then deleted. These covered:
- markAsPaid called on two stale copies of the same order
- markAsPaid called again on an already-shipped order
- the job run against an unpaid order
- a 201 without an id, then a retry
- cancellation, a 422 and a 503, each through a real database queue worker

Ranking:
1. impl-1 ranks first. It is the cleanest and most modern: queue attributes, enums, #[Fillable], 429 handling that honours Retry-After, an atomic exactly-once email claim, and excellent tests. Its weaknesses are a non-atomic markAsPaid guard (two stale instances push 2 jobs) and no WithoutOverlapping lock. Only the Idempotency-Key header stops a duplicate POST in that narrow race.
2. impl-4 ranks second. It is the most robust on the focus area: an atomic conditional-update markAsPaid, a 201 without an id treated as permanent to avoid duplicates, Retry-After capped at 120s, WithoutOverlapping, and the best tests (a real rate-limit test, afterCommit on the DB queue). But it uses string constants instead of enums, the legacy job traits and property-style config, and carries more ceremony and comments. It also sends the email before recording it, so a crash in between re-sends it.
3. impl-3 ranks third. It is modern and safe against concurrency (refresh() plus WithoutOverlapping), but the job never checks the paid status (probe: it ships unpaid orders) and it treats 429 as a generic exception.
4. impl-2 ranks last because of a real state bug. markAsPaid has no guard, so calling it again on a shipped order resets shipment_status to pending forever and dispatches a new job each time. Its email handling is also non-atomic.
